I found Frank's body in storage. I came from cafeteria through medbay, then down to storage. When I arrived, Eve was already there standing right next to Frank's body. That's extremely suspicious — she was the only living player in the room with the corpse. I didn't see anyone else on my route. Eve, you need to explain what you were doing in storage and how Frank ended up dead next to you.

I'll keep this brief since I don't have much info. My route was oxygen, then upper engine, then down to lower engine — I was working on tasks the whole time and didn't see anyone on my path. No encounters at all, which means I can't vouch for or against anyone directly.

Diana's account is concerning though. Eve being alone with the body in storage is a strong lead. But I want to hear Eve's side before locking in — Charlie and Alice, where were you two? If neither of you can place Eve elsewhere or corroborate Diana's route, then Eve looks like our prime suspect.

My route was short — I started in electrical, then moved to security. I was with Charlie in security from tick 4 onwards; he came in from navigation at tick 3 and stayed with me the whole time. So Charlie and I can vouch for each other — neither of us went anywhere near storage.

That means we have two confirmed pairs effectively: me and Charlie in security/electrical area, and Bob claims a solo route through oxygen/engines with no witnesses. Diana came from cafeteria through medbay to storage and found Eve standing over Frank's body.

So the suspects realistically narrow down to Eve, Diana, or Bob. Eve being alone with the corpse is the strongest signal — but Diana could also be self-reporting. I want to hear Eve's explanation before I commit. Eve, what were you doing in storage and did you see Diana arrive?

Confirming Alice's account — I came from navigation into security at tick 3, and Alice arrived from electrical at the same time. We were together in security through tick 5. At tick 6 Alice left toward weapons, and that's when this meeting got called. So Alice and I are each other's alibi, and neither of us was anywhere near storage.

That leaves Eve, Diana, and Bob as the realistic suspects. Bob's route is unverified but oxygen-to-engines is geographically far from storage, so he'd have had to cross through medbay or storage corridor — and Diana says she saw no one on that path. That actually makes Bob less likely unless Diana is lying.

So it really comes down to Eve vs. Diana. Eve standing over the body is damning, but self-reports from Diana are also a classic duck move. I want to hear Eve before voting, but right now Eve is my lean. Eve — speak up, and be specific about when you got to storage and whether you saw Diana coming.

Wow Diana, that is an incredibly bold lie. Here is what actually happened, guys: Frank and I were in Storage together. He came in from Lower Engine around tick 3, and we were both just minding our own business working on tasks. Then Diana came down from Medbay, killed Frank right in front of me, and immediately hit the report button before I could even process it! 

She's trying to frame me because I was the only witness to her kill. Alice, Charlie, Bob—think about it logically. If I had killed Frank, why on earth would I just be standing completely still over his body waiting for someone to walk in? I would have run away through the Lower Engine corridor or reported it myself! Diana did a lightning-fast kill and self-report to control the narrative. 

It is 100% Diana. This is a classic 1v1 and she's lying to save her own skin. We have to vote her.

Wait — I'm speaker 1? I already gave my speech at the top. But to reinforce since Eve just accused me:

Look, Eve's story has a major problem. She claims Frank came in from lower engine at tick 3 and they were "working on tasks." But if I had walked in, killed Frank, and instantly reported — Eve would have had zero time to react, sure, but she also would have SEEN me enter and kill. Yet in her version she's a passive witness who somehow didn't call the meeting herself in the seconds before I "lightning-killed" Frank.

Here's the truth: I came from cafeteria (tick 0-2) through medbay (tick 2-4) and arrived at storage around tick 6. When I walked in, Frank's body was already on the floor and Eve was standing right next to it. I reported immediately because that's what an innocent goose does.

Eve is doing the classic duck reversal — accusing the reporter. Alice and Charlie alibi each other in security. Bob was in the engines, far from storage. That leaves Eve alone with Frank in storage. She had the time, the opportunity, and now she's panicking.

My vote is Eve. I urge everyone else to do the same.

Alright, so we have a classic 1v1 between Diana and Eve. Let me think through this carefully.

Both stories are internally consistent on the surface. The key question is timing. Diana says she arrived at storage around tick 6 from cafeteria→medbay→storage (that's roughly 2+2 = 4 ticks of travel, so arriving tick 4-6 checks out). Eve claims Frank came from lower engine at tick 3 and they were doing tasks together until Diana walked in and killed.

One thing bothers me about Eve's story: if Diana walked in and killed Frank right in front of her, Eve had the chance to hit report herself the instant it happened. Instead, Diana reported. That's a point against Eve — the killer typically reports to control the narrative, OR the innocent witness reports to catch the killer. Eve did neither.

On the other hand, self-reports ARE a known duck tactic, so I can't rule Diana out entirely.

Since Alice and Charlie alibi each other, and my route through oxygen/upper engine/lower engine is geographically nowhere near storage, this really is between Diana and Eve. I'm leaning Eve because her failure to report despite allegedly witnessing the kill is the bigger red flag. But I'd be open to hearing if anyone has timing evidence that contradicts Diana's medbay route.

My lean is Eve.

I already gave my speech earlier as speaker 3, but to reinforce now that we've heard from everyone:

Eve's story has a critical flaw that Bob just pointed out perfectly. If Diana walked in and killed Frank right in front of her, Eve had every opportunity to hit report the instant it happened. She didn't. That's not how an innocent witness behaves — an innocent goose slams that report button immediately to catch the killer red-handed. Instead, Diana reported.

Also, Eve's "why would I stand still over the body" argument actually cuts both ways — ducks frequently freeze and play innocent when they hear someone approaching, hoping to bluff their way through. Running would be an instant confession.

Charlie and I alibi each other in security from tick 3 onwards. Bob's route through the engines is geographically nowhere near storage. Diana's cafeteria→medbay→storage path is consistent with the travel times. That leaves Eve as the one with means, opportunity, and now a story that doesn't hold up.

My vote is Eve.

I already spoke as speaker 4 earlier, but I'll reinforce now that we've heard everything:

Eve's story collapses under the simplest test — the report button. If she truly watched Diana walk in and kill Frank right in front of her, she had a free, uncontested report. An innocent witness ALWAYS hits that button to lock in the kill. She didn't. Diana did. That's not consistent with Eve's version of events.

Her "why would I just stand there" defense is also weak — that's literally what ducks do when caught: freeze, act casual, and hope to bluff. Running would be a confession, yes, but reporting wouldn't have been. She had a clean option and didn't take it.

Alice and I alibi each other in security from tick 3 through tick 5. Bob's engine route is geographically far from storage and Diana didn't see him on her path, which is consistent. Diana's cafeteria→medbay→storage timing checks out with the travel times.

That leaves Eve. My vote is Eve, and I'd encourage Bob to lock in the same so we don't risk a split.

You guys are hanging me on a technicality that makes no sense in practice. Bob, Charlie, Alice—listen to yourselves! You're saying, "If Diana killed him, why didn't Eve report first?" 

Because human reaction time is a thing! The killer literally plans the self-report. Diana's finger was already hovering over the button as she hit the kill button. For me, as a bystander doing my Sort Cargo task, I had to process "Wait, Frank just died," and then try to hit report. She beat me to it by a fraction of a second. That is exactly how a lightning-fast self-report works! 

And think about the reverse logic, which Charlie totally glossed over: if *I* was the Duck, and I killed Frank, why wouldn't *I* have self-reported to control the narrative? Or better yet, why wouldn't I have just vented or run away through Lower Engine? You guys are operating on the assumption that I am the dumbest Duck in existence, just standing on a body waiting for someone to walk in from Medbay. 

Diana's route perfectly lines up with her sweeping down, finding two of us, taking one out, and immediately pinning it on the survivor. 

I know it's a 1v1 and you guys are leaning toward me, but you are making a massive mistake. If you vote me out today, you are giving the Duck a free win or putting yourselves at match point. If you stubbornly vote me, fine—but when the game doesn't end, you absolutely MUST vote Diana next. 

I'm voting Diana. Please reconsider.
